verification.notes: The ICTY’s historical account traces the wars to Yugoslavia’s political and economic crisis, breakup, and ethnonationalist conflict. A detailed U.S. policy history shows Washington initially held back and intervened later to help end the Bosnian war. These records contradict the broad assertion that the United States was behind the Yugoslav wars.

sources.title: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia: The Conflicts
sources.relevance: Authoritative history attributes the wars to Yugoslavia’s breakup, political crisis, and nationalist conflict rather than a U.S.-directed origin.

sources.title: Brookings: Decision to Intervene—How the War in Bosnia Ended
sources.relevance: Documents initial U.S. reluctance followed by later intervention and diplomacy, contradicting the allegation that the United States was behind the wars.

records.text: Owens cited reports by DynCorp investigator Kathryn Bolkovac and employee Ben Johnston alleging that DynCorp personnel in Bosnia purchased underage women and facilitated sex trafficking; Owens said both whistleblowers were fired after reporting the abuses.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

verification.notes: The cited book was identified, but no accessible passage verified this exact four-country list.
